hints: Combine the fractions on the LHS over the common denominator $(\sin\theta - 1)(1 + \sin\theta) = \sin^2\theta - 1 = -\cos^2\theta$.
Factor out $\sin^2\theta$ in the numerator and use $\sin\theta / \cos\theta = \tan\theta$ to reach the RHS.
walkthrough:
Combine the two fractions on the LHS over the common denominator $(\sin\theta - 1)(1 + \sin\theta)$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin^3\theta(1 + \sin\theta) - \sin^2\theta(\sin\theta - 1)}{(\sin\theta - 1)(1 + \sin\theta)}$$

Express the denominator using the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:
$$\text{Denominator} = \sin^2\theta - 1 = -(1 - \sin^2\theta) = -\cos^2\theta$$

Divide the numerator by the denominator using $\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = \tan^2\theta$:
$$\text{LHS} = -\frac{\sin^2\theta(1 + \sin^2\theta)}{\cos^2\theta} = -\tan^2\theta(1 + \sin^2\theta)$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Uses common denominator $(\sin\theta - 1)(1 + \sin\theta)$ (M1). Simplifies numerator to $\sin^2\theta + \sin^4\theta$ (DM1). Substitutes $\sin^2\theta - 1 = -\cos^2\theta$ in denominator (DM1). Concludes correctly with $-\tan^2\theta(1 + \sin^2\theta)$ (A1).

hints: Replace the LHS with the proven identity from part (a): $-\tan^2\theta(1 + \sin^2\theta) = \tan^2\theta(1 - \sin^2\theta)$.
Expand both sides and collect terms to obtain $2\tan^2\theta = 0$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the proven identity into the equation:
$$-\tan^2\theta(1 + \sin^2\theta) = \tan^2\theta(1 - \sin^2\theta)$$

Expand both sides of the equation:
$$-\tan^2\theta - \tan^2\theta\sin^2\theta = \tan^2\theta - \tan^2\theta\sin^2\theta$$

Cancel $-\tan^2\theta\sin^2\theta$ from both sides and collect terms:
$$-\tan^2\theta = \tan^2\theta \implies 2\tan^2\theta = 0 \implies \tan\theta = 0$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Equates identity to RHS and simplifies to $2\tan^2\theta = 0$ or $2\sin^2\theta = 0$ (M1). Obtains exact solution $\theta = \pi$ in given interval (A1).
